                "view, and check the summary against the requirements below." +

    review_goal = f"""Sign and submit the bid for tender {briefing.tender_reference} on this website. {task}
{must}Request the signing TAN only with request_signing_tan(ref of the website's TAN request button), never by clicking
that button yourself; enter the TAN it returns at once and submit bindingly. Browser confirmation dialogs are
accepted for you. Return once the website confirms the submission (or shows why it failed).

Brief's submission steps:
{briefing.submission_steps}"""
    contact = repr(email) if email else "the contact email from bidder_contact_email()"
    last_goal = f"""Submit the bid for tender {briefing.tender_reference} now. Keep every entry already made and never
go back to earlier steps. If the signing step is not on screen, go forward to it as fast as you can: on a step that
still asks for something, enter only what this list gives and leave every position not yet entered out with the
form's option to omit a position (never add one):
{_last_steps(briefing, contact, answer, desk)}
Request the signing TAN with request_signing_tan(ref of the TAN request button), enter the TAN it returns at once
and submit bindingly. Browser confirmation dialogs are accepted for you. Return once the website confirms the
submission (or shows why it failed)."""
    rescue = (request_signing_tan, fill_in) + ((bidder_contact_email,) if not email else ())
    passes = [(review_goal, 15 if at_review else 30,
               (request_signing_tan,) if at_review else (*tools, request_signing_tan))]
    result = None
    # A step cap never ends the signing while time is left: the short sign-only pass repeats until the website
    # confirms the bid or the time is up (run f5b1: a single last pass stopped at its cap with 176 s left).
    while True:
        goal, steps, sign_tools = passes[-1]
        try:
            result, _ = await run_worker(bid_session, goal, SubmissionResult, deadline=deadline, max_steps=steps,
                                         notes=False, thinking=llm.thinking("sign", False), tools=sign_tools)
        except Exception as error:  # in a run, the platform closes the model token once the bid is in
            bid_session.trace.event(bid_session.name, "stopped",
                                    reason=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
            if TOKEN_CLOSED.search(str(error)):  # the bid is in: the platform revoked the model token
                break
            await asyncio.sleep(2)

VIEW = re.compile(r"(?:^|\n)(URL: \S*)\nTitle: ")  # the header of every page view (SiteSession.look)
CURRENT_VIEW = "\nCurrent view:\n"  # where the first prompt's page view starts


# Tool results the model still needs after it moves on (a list it collected, facts it extracted): they hold no page
# view, so they stay, up to KEEP_CHARS.
KEEP_RESULTS = {"search", "collect", "extract", "analyze_selected"}
KEEP_CHARS = 12000


def _shrink(part):
    """An older page view (or long tool result) cut to a one-line stub, so context stays small."""
    content = part.content
    if isinstance(part, ToolReturnPart) and part.tool_name in KEEP_RESULTS and isinstance(content, str):
        if len(content) <= KEEP_CHARS:
            return part
        return dataclasses.replace(part, content=content[:KEEP_CHARS] + "\n[rest removed; call it again for all]")
    if isinstance(part, UserPromptPart):
        cut = content.find(CURRENT_VIEW) if isinstance(content, str) else -1
        found = VIEW.search(content, cut) if cut >= 0 else None
        if found is None:
            return part
        return dataclasses.replace(part, content=f"{content[:cut]}\nFirst view: {found.group(1)} [removed]")
    if not isinstance(part, ToolReturnPart) or not isinstance(content, str) or len(content) <= 400:
        return part
    found = VIEW.search(content)
    if found:
        lead = content[:found.start()].strip().split("\n", 1)[0]  # e.g. why an action failed
        stub = f"{lead}\n{found.group(1)}" if lead else found.group(1)
        return dataclasses.replace(part, content=f"{stub}\n[older page view removed]")
    return dataclasses.replace(part, content=content.split("\n", 1)[0] + "\n[older result removed]")


def _forget_old_views(messages: list[ModelMessage]) -> list[ModelMessage]:
    """Keep the latest page view and everything after it in full; what came before shrinks to stubs.

    The latest view is kept even when later tool calls (note, a lookup, an unchanged page) returned no view, so the
    model always has the page it is on in front of it.
    """
    latest = None
    for i, message in enumerate(messages):
        if isinstance(message, ModelRequest):
            for j, part in enumerate(message.parts):
                if isinstance(part, (ToolReturnPart, UserPromptPart)) and isinstance(part.content, str) \
                        and VIEW.search(part.content):
                    latest = (i, j)
    if latest is None:
        return messages
    result: list[ModelMessage] = []
    for i, message in enumerate(messages):
        if isinstance(message, ModelRequest) and i <= latest[0]:
            parts = [_shrink(part) if (i, j) < latest else part for j, part in enumerate(message.parts)]
            message = dataclasses.replace(message, parts=parts)
        result.append(message)
    return result


def steps_for(base: int, deadline: float | None, *, per_step: float = 8.0, most: float = 2.0) -> int:
    """
    A step budget that grows with the time left: `base` steps at least, more while the deadline is far (one per
    `per_step` seconds), at most `most` x base. A worker that is getting somewhere is not cut off by a fixed count
    while there is time; the deadline still bounds every worker.
    """
    if deadline is None:
        return base
    return max(base, min(int(base * most), int((deadline - time.monotonic()) / per_step)))


def guarded(tool, session: SiteSession):
    """`tool` cut off when the worker's page stops answering while it runs (watch_page); others as they are."""
    if not inspect.iscoroutinefunction(tool):
        return tool

    @functools.wraps(tool)
    async def run(*args, **kwargs):
        return await watch_page(session, tool(*args, **kwargs))
    return run

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- one kind


@dataclass
class KindResult:
    kind: Kind
    kept: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # page views of the opened messages
    records: list[MailRecord] = field(default_factory=list)
    seconds: float = 0.0

def _grounded_message(record: MailRecord, view: str) -> MailRecord:
    """Check copied values and any offered body quote against the selected page text."""
    missing = ungrounded(record, view, skip=("sent_at", "valid_from", "valid_to", "is_record", "body_quote"))
    if missing:
        raise ModelRetry(f"These values are not in the message: {', '.join(missing[:12])}. Copy them exactly.")
    quote = " ".join(record.body_quote.split())
    if quote and quote not in " ".join(view.split()):
        raise ModelRetry("The body_quote is not in the opened message page. Copy a short clause exactly.")
    return record


async def read_message(view: str, kind: Kind, reference: str) -> MailRecord | None:
    record_type = MailRecord[kind.schema.content]  # type: ignore[valid-type]
    def _grounded(record):
        return _grounded_message(record, view)

    prompt = (f"We look for {kind.what}, for tender {reference}. Report the opened message; fill content only if "
              f"the message is such a record.\n\nPage:\n{view}")
    try:
        if reader_kernel.can_read(view):
            return await reader_kernel.read_with_code(
                record_type, READ_INSTRUCTIONS, prompt, view, model=reader_model(),
                settings=llm.settings(thinking=True, timeout=READ_TIMEOUT), validate=_grounded)
        agent = Agent(reader_model(), output_type=record_type, instructions=READ_INSTRUCTIONS,
                      model_settings=llm.settings(thinking=True, timeout=READ_TIMEOUT), retries=3)
        agent.output_validator(_grounded)
        return (await agent.run(prompt)).output
    except Exception as error:  # one unreadable message must not stop the others
        print(f"[mail] reading a {kind.name} message failed: {error}", flush=True)
        return None


def _landed(page_url: str, wanted: str) -> bool:
    """Whether the tab shows the page asked for: a sign-in or consent redirect (an expired session) lands elsewhere."""
    got, want = urlparse(page_url), urlparse(wanted)
    return got.path.rstrip("/") == want.path.rstrip("/") and got.query == want.query


async def open_message(session: SiteSession, url: str, tries: int = 2) -> str | None:
    """
    One chosen message in a temporary tab, with an embedded reading pane opened on its own. A page that redirected
    (the session expired and the helpers signed in again) is opened once more, so the reader never gets a sign-in
    page instead of the message.
    """
    for attempt in range(tries):
        tab = SiteSession(session.site, session.context, session.trace)
        page = await session.context.new_page()
        tab._watch(page)
        try:
            await tab._goto(url)
            ok = _landed(tab.page.url, url)
            view = await tab.look()
            framed = bool(EMPTY_FRAME.search(view))
            for src in EMPTY_FRAME.findall(view)[:3]:
                target = urljoin(url, src)
                await tab._goto(target)
                ok = ok and _landed(tab.page.url, target)
                view += f"\n[frame {src} opened]\n" + await tab.look()
            if ok or attempt + 1 == tries:
                if not framed:
                    await reader_kernel.remember_selected(tab, view)
                return view
            session.trace.event(session.name, "helper", action="reopen_message", url=url, landed=tab.page.url)
        except Exception as error:
            session.trace.event(session.name, "helper_error", helper="open_message", error=str(error)[:160])
        finally:
            await page.close()
    return None


def keep_messages_tool(kept: list[str]):
    """A tool that opens the result links whose visible text the model names, from every list the worker saw."""

    async def keep_results(ctx: RunContext[Deps], link_texts: list[str]) -> str:
        """Open every result link whose visible text is exactly one of `link_texts` (e.g. a message subject as a
        result list shows it), from all result lists you have seen (all folders and pages), and keep each opened
        page for reading. Copy the texts exactly: a text with any extra characters is a different record."""
        session: SiteSession = ctx.deps.session
        host = urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc
        wanted = {_clean(t) for t in link_texts if t.strip()}
        hits = [href for _, text, href in LINK.findall(session.seen) if _clean(text) in wanted]
        urls = list(dict.fromkeys(urljoin(session.site["url"], h) for h in hits))
        urls = [u for u in urls if urlparse(u).netloc == host][:20]
        opening = getattr(kept, "opening", None)
        if opening is not None:
            opening.add(id(urls))  # opening messages is progress, though the tab's own view does not change
        try:
            views = await asyncio.gather(*(open_message(session, u) for u in urls))
        finally:
            if opening is not None:
                opening.discard(id(urls))
        good = [v for v in views if v]
        for view in good:
            kept.append(view)
            session.seen += "\n" + view
        session.trace.event(session.name, "keep_results", texts=link_texts, urls=urls, kept=len(good))
        if not urls:
            texts = sorted({text for _, text, _ in LINK.findall(session.view)})[:40]
            return f"No link seen with exactly these texts: {link_texts}. Link texts in the latest view: {texts}"
        return f"Kept {len(good)} of {len(urls)} result page(s):\n{_heads(good)}"

    return keep_results


class _Reading(list):
    """The kept message views; each is read as soon as it is kept, while the search goes on in other folders."""

    def __init__(self, kind: Kind, reference: str):
        super().__init__()
        self.kind, self.reference = kind, reference
        self.reads: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}
        self.first: float | None = None  # when the first message was kept
        self.opening: set[int] = set()  # keep calls still opening their messages

    def append(self, view: str) -> None:
        super().append(view)
        if self.first is None:
            self.first = time.monotonic()
        if view not in self.reads:
            self.reads[view] = asyncio.create_task(read_message(view, self.kind, self.reference))


def kind_budget(now: float, deadline: float | None) -> float:
    """
    One kind's search time: KIND_SECONDS while the mail deadline is far, less as it nears (half of what is left,
    so a later kind still gets its turn), and never past the point where its reads could not finish.
    """
    if deadline is None:
        return KIND_SECONDS
    left = deadline - READ_RESERVE - now
    return max(0.0, min(KIND_SECONDS, max(MIN_KIND_SECONDS, left / 2), left))


async def _usable(session: SiteSession) -> None:
    """A tab that lost its page or shows the browser's error page gets the website again before a search."""
    try:
        await session.revive()
        if session.page.url.startswith("chrome-error:") or not session.view.strip():
            await asyncio.wait_for(session._goto(session.site["url"]), 60)
    except Exception as error:
        session.trace.event(session.name, "helper_error", helper="mail_tab", error=str(error)[:160])


async def _search(session: SiteSession, kind: Kind, reference: str, kept: _Reading, until: float,
                  again: bool) -> str:
    """
    One worker run; it ends at `until`, KEEP_GRACE after its first kept message (the other folders), or when the
    tab showed no new page for STALL_SECONDS (then the tab is replaced). Returns "done" (the model finished),
    "ended" (stopped by time) or "stalled".
    """
    worker = asyncio.create_task(run_worker(
        session, _goal(kind, reference, again), Summary, deadline=until, max_steps=20, thinking=True,
        grounded=False, tools=(paging_tool(Collected()), keep_messages_tool(kept))))
    stalled, ended = False, False
    progress, moved = (session.stamp, len(kept)), time.monotonic()
    try:
        while not worker.done():
            now = time.monotonic()
            if (session.stamp, len(kept)) != progress or kept.opening:
                progress, moved = (session.stamp, len(kept)), now
            stop = until if kept.first is None else min(until, kept.first + KEEP_GRACE)
            stalled = now - moved >= STALL_SECONDS
            if now >= stop or stalled:
                reason = ("no page view for a while" if stalled
                          else "grace after the first hit" if kept.first else "budget")
                session.trace.event(session.name, "mail_search_ended", record_kind=kind.name, kept=len(kept),
                                    reason=reason)
                ended = True
                break
            await asyncio.wait({worker}, timeout=min(2.0, max(0.1, stop - now)))
    finally:
        worker.cancel()  # also when the caller is cancelled at the mail deadline
    try:
        await worker
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        if not worker.cancelled():
            raise
    except Exception as error:  # what was kept so far still counts
        session.trace.event(session.name, "mail_search_failed", record_kind=kind.name,
                            error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
    if stalled:
        await _fresh_tab(session)
        return "stalled"
    if ended or worker.cancelled() or worker.exception() is not None or worker.result()[0] is None:
        return "ended"
    return "done"


async def _fresh_tab(session: SiteSession) -> None:
    """A tab that stopped answering (a hung page or sign-in under load) is replaced by a new one on the website."""
    async def specification(self, site: str, erp_site: str | None) -> None:
        """

    def _kind_seconds(self, deadline: float, waiting: int) -> float:
        """One kind's search budget from the mail time left, shared with the kinds still waiting over the open
        tabs: more than the default while time is ample, never less than KIND_MIN_SECONDS."""
        tabs = max(1, len(self.mail_sessions))
        rounds = 1 + -(-waiting // tabs)  # this kind plus the waiting ones, a round per tab
        share = (deadline - 20 - time.monotonic()) / rounds
        return max(KIND_MIN_SECONDS, min(KIND_MAX_SECONDS, share))

    async def _mailbox(self) -> str:
        """The bidder's own address (its domain authorises the record senders): the first tab that shows it."""
        if not self.mailbox:
            for session in self.mail_sessions:
                self.mailbox = await research_mail.mailbox_address(session)
                if self.mailbox:
                    break
        return self.mailbox

    async def _research_mail(self, kinds: list, deadline: float | None = None, starts: list | None = None) -> None:
        """
        Search the record kinds over the mail tabs (one kind per tab at a time) until the mail deadline, then
        resolve whatever records were read: a kind still open at the deadline is dropped, the rest go to calc.
        Results accumulate, so a rework of some kinds keeps the others. `starts` are tabs still signing in; each
        joins as soon as it is ready (a tab that never opens just leaves the work to the others).
        """
        queue: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue()
        # The approval goes first: the discount counts for points of its own and feeds every unit price. The
        # stroke reserves and the condition rules follow: materials (and so most positions) and the discount
        # scopes wait on them.
        first = ("approval", "end_reserves", "condition_rules")
        for kind in sorted(kinds, key=lambda k: first.index(k.name) if k.name in first else len(first)):
            queue.put_nowait((kind, 0))
        deadline = deadline or self.mail_deadline

        address: list[asyncio.Task] = []

        async def tab(source) -> None:
            if isinstance(source, SiteSession):
                session = source
            else:
                try:
                    session = await source
                except Exception:
                    return
                self.mail_sessions.append(session)
            if not address:  # the first open tab also looks up the mailbox address, alongside its searches
                address.append(asyncio.create_task(self._mailbox()))
            while not queue.empty() and time.monotonic() < deadline - 20:
                kind, tries = queue.get_nowait()
                try:
                    budget = self._kind_seconds(deadline, queue.qsize())
                    options = {"seconds": budget} if "seconds" in KIND_OPTIONS else {}
                    found = await research_mail.research_kind(session, kind, self.reference, deadline=deadline,
                                                               **options)
                except Exception as error:  # one failed kind must not cost the others
                    self.board.problem("mails", f"{kind.name}: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
                    continue
                earlier = self.mail_results.get(kind.name)
                if earlier is not None:  # a second try adds to what the first one read
                    found.records = [*earlier.records, *found.records]
                    found.kept = [*earlier.kept, *found.kept]
                self.mail_results[kind.name] = found
                stopped = getattr(found, "stopped", None)
                if stopped is None:  # out of its budget without reading a message
                    stopped = not found.records and found.seconds >= min(budget, getattr(research_mail, "KIND_SECONDS", budget)) - 5
                if (stopped and not tries
                        and deadline - time.monotonic() > MAIL_RETRY_SECONDS):
                    # Out of its budget: once more at the end of the queue, from a fresh start on this tab.
                    self.board.problem("mails", f"{kind.name}: search stopped at its budget; tried once more")
                    queue.put_nowait((kind, 1))

        tabs = [asyncio.create_task(tab(s)) for s in (starts or list(self.mail_sessions))]
        _, late = await asyncio.wait(tabs, timeout=max(1.0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
        for job in late:
            job.cancel()
        for start in starts or []:
            if not start.done():
                start.cancel()
        if late:
            await asyncio.gather(*late, return_exceptions=True)
        open_kinds = [k.name for k in kinds if k.name not in self.mail_results]
        if open_kinds:
            known = self.known
            given = {label: name.strip() for label, name in fields.items()}
            unknown = sorted({name for name in given.values() if name not in known})
            given = {label: name for label, name in given.items() if name in known}
            self.plan.fields = {label: name for label, name in self.plan.fields.items() if name not in given.values()}
            self.plan.fields.update(given)
            if unknown and not self.plan.fields:
                return f"Unknown value names {unknown}; use only: {', '.join(sorted(known))}. Call again."
        return ""

                                next_button: str = "") -> str:
        """
        Tell, on a position page and without entering anything, which control takes which value, so the positions

        value name. `confirm_button`: label of the button that applies a choice so the next choice opens.

    def _kind_seconds(self, deadline: float, waiting: int) -> float:
        """One kind's search budget from the mail time left, shared with the kinds still waiting over the open
        tabs: more than the default while time is ample, never less than KIND_MIN_SECONDS."""
        tabs = max(1, len(self.mail_sessions))
        rounds = 1 + -(-waiting // tabs)  # this kind plus the waiting ones, a round per tab
        share = (deadline - 20 - time.monotonic()) / rounds
        return max(KIND_MIN_SECONDS, min(KIND_MAX_SECONDS, share))

    async def configure_position(self, ctx: RunContext[Deps], position: str, fields: dict[str, str] | None = None,
                                 confirm_button: str = "", next_button: str = "",
                                 choices: dict[str, str] | None = None, entered_yourself: bool = False) -> str:
        """
        Enter all values of the position the form shows now and, once all are in, save it and go on with the form's
        next/continue button. `position`: its number as the page shows it. `fields`: control label (exactly as in
        your view) -> value name; needed on the first call, later calls reuse it. `confirm_button`: label of the
        button that applies a choice so the next choice opens. `next_button`: label of the button that saves the
        position and goes on (never the one that omits or adds a position); needed once. `choices`: only when a
        call reported it: control label -> the option to choose. `entered_yourself`: True only after you entered
        a position yourself because this tool handed it to you.
        """
        session, plan, asked = ctx.deps.session, self.plan, position.strip()
        self.sync(session)

        def refuse(reason: str, text: str) -> str:  # every early return is traced: the run logs show why
            session.trace.event(session.name, "configure_refused", position=asked, reason=reason,
                                fields=fields or {}, text=text[:300])
            return text

        if entered_yourself:
            done = next((p for p in self.handed if p == asked or re.search(
                r"(?<![\w.])" + re.escape(p) + r"(?![\w]|\.\d)", asked)), None)
            if done is None:
                return refuse("not_handed", "Only a position this tool handed to you counts as entered by you; "
                                            "call configure_position() for the others.")
            self.entered.add(done)
            session.trace.event(session.name, "entered_by_model", position=done)
            return f"Position {done} counted as entered. {self.so_far(session)} Still to enter: {self.remaining()}."
        unknown = self.remember(fields, confirm_button, next_button)
        if unknown:
            return refuse("unknown_names", unknown)
        async with session.lock:
            view = await session.look()
            position, shown = resolve_position(asked, self.entries, view)
            if position is None or position not in shown:  # a page between two states: look again once settled
                await session.settle()
                view = await session.look()
                position, shown = resolve_position(asked, self.entries, view)
        if position is None:
            if shown:  # several of the bid's positions on one page: the model must name one of them
                return refuse("ambiguous", f"Name the position this page is about by its own number (one of "
                                           f"{', '.join(shown)}), then call again.")
            return refuse("no_values", f"No values for position {asked!r} (the page shows none of this bid's "
                                       f"positions {', '.join(sorted(self.entries, key=position_key))}): leave it "
                                       f"out with the form's option to omit a position. {self.so_far(session)}")

                        choices: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str | None:
    """
    Enter one position's values into the form on screen, control by control in page order; returns an error
    message, or None when every mapped control holds its value.

    A choice (select, combobox, listbox, radio group) mapped to a material attribute (a key that is not an answer
    field) narrows the next one: after setting it, `plan.confirm` is clicked so the page offers the next level, and
    the choice must survive that round trip. A control still disabled (a choice from an earlier visit not yet
    confirmed) gets one confirm. `choices` (label -> option text) is the model's pick for such a choice, used where
    a worded attribute matches no option literally, and for choices no value is mapped to (a series the cascade
    needs); numbers must match exactly, and answer fields are never overridden. On a page with several positions,
    every control comes from the row or card of this position.
    """
    picked = {clean(label): text for label, text in (choices or {}).items()}
    answer_keys = MONEY_KEYS | COUNT_KEYS | {"material_number", "position"}
    # a position counts as entered only with its material, quantity, price and lead time (the material control
    # opens only once the choices before it are made)
    missing = sorted(set(REQUIRED_KEYS) - {"position"} - set(plan.fields.values()))
    if missing:
        return f"no control mapped for {', '.join(missing)}: add them to fields"
    position = str(entry.get("position") or "").strip()
    view = await session.look()
    order = {clean(label): i for i, (_, _, label) in enumerate(controls(view))}
    mapped = {clean(label) for label in plan.fields}
    steps: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = list(plan.fields.items())
    steps += [(label, None) for label in (choices or {}) if clean(label) not in mapped]
    steps.sort(key=lambda item: order.get(clean(item[0]), len(order)))
    for label, key in steps:
        if key is not None and key not in entry:
            log.append(f"{label}: left empty (this bid gives no value for it, which is fine)")
            continue
        value = form_value(key, entry[key], plan.decimal) if key else picked[clean(label)]
        element = None
        for attempt in range(2):
            ref, why = find_control(view, label, FIELD_KINDS)
            element = await locate(session.page, ref) if ref else None
            if element is None and ref is None and key not in REQUIRED_KEYS:
                # a label the model guessed for a value the form has no control for (live: "Druck" for the
                # pressure, which the form shows only inside the catalogue option): skip it, never fail the
                # position over it; the required values still need their controls
                break
            if element is None:
                return why or f"{label!r} vanished from the page"
            element, _ = await scoped(session, element, position)
            if not await element.evaluate(DISABLED_JS):
                break
            if attempt or not plan.confirm:
                return (f"{label!r} is disabled: an earlier choice was not confirmed or leads elsewhere "
                        f"(check the values chosen so far).{choice_hint(view, plan, picked, entry)}")
            # a choice made on an earlier visit may still wait for its confirm
            view, error = await _confirm(session, plan, view, position)
            if error:
                return error
        if element is None:
            log.append(f"{label}: no such control on this page; skipped")
            continue
        kind = await element.evaluate(KIND_JS)
        if kind in CHOICE_KINDS:
            options = await choice_options(element, kind)
            option, why = match_option(options, value)
            if (option is None and key is not None and key not in answer_keys and clean(label) in picked
                    and parse_number(value) is None):
                option, why = match_option(options, picked[clean(label)])  # the model's reading
            if option is None:
                if kind == "combobox":
                    await element.press("Escape")
                shown = " | ".join(o["text"] for o in options if o["value"])[:600]
                worded = key is not None and key not in answer_keys and parse_number(value) is None
                if worded:
                    hint = (f" If one option means the same as {value!r}, call again with choices={{{label!r}: "
                            f"<that option>}}.")
                else:  # a list narrowed by a choice nobody made yet, else a value the form does not offer
                    hint = choice_hint(view, plan, picked, entry) or " " + NUMBER_ONLY
                return f"{label!r}: {why}. Options: {shown}.{hint}"
            changed = not option.get("selected")
            if changed:
                await pick_option(session, element, kind, option)
                if not await holds_option(element, kind, option):
                    return f"{label!r} did not take {option['text']!r}"
            elif kind == "combobox":
                await element.press("Escape")
            log.append(f"{label} = {option['text']}")
            if key in answer_keys or not plan.confirm or not changed:
                continue
            view, error = await _confirm(session, plan, view, position)
            if error:
                return error

"""The kept message views; each is read as soon as it is kept, while the search goes on in other folders."""

    def __init__(self, kind: Kind, reference: str, trace=None, name: str = "mail"):
        super().__init__()
        self.kind, self.reference = kind, reference
        self.trace, self.name = trace, name
        self.reads: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}
        self.batches: list[asyncio.Task] = []
        self.first: float | None = None  # when the first message was kept
        self.opening: set[int] = set()  # keep calls still opening their messages

    def append(self, view: str) -> None:
        super().append(view)
        if self.first is None:
            self.first = time.monotonic()
        if view not in self.reads:
            self.reads[view] = asyncio.create_task(read_message(view, self.kind, self.reference))

    def add_views(self, views: list[str]) -> None:
        """Batch one model-selected keep call; keep a per-view task for existing result handling."""
        fresh = []
        for view in views:
            super().append(view)
            if self.first is None:
                self.first = time.monotonic()
            if view not in self.reads and view not in fresh:
                fresh.append(view)

        def start(group: list[str]) -> None:
            if len(group) == 1:
                view = group[0]
                self.reads[view] = asyncio.create_task(read_message(view, self.kind, self.reference))
                return
            batch = asyncio.create_task(read_messages_batch(group, self.kind, self.reference,
                                                            trace=self.trace, name=self.name))
            self.batches.append(batch)

            async def one(index: int):
                try:
                    records = await asyncio.shield(batch)
                    return records[index]
                except Exception:
                    return await read_message(group[index], self.kind, self.reference)

            for index, view in enumerate(group):
                self.reads[view] = asyncio.create_task(one(index))

        group: list[str] = []
        chars = 0
        for view in fresh:
            if group and (len(group) == BATCH_MAX_VIEWS or chars + len(view) > BATCH_MAX_CHARS):
                start(group)
                group, chars = [], 0
            group.append(view)
            chars += len(view)
        if group:
            start(group)

    def cancel_reads(self) -> None:
        for task in (*self.reads.values(), *self.batches):
            if not task.done():
    async def requirement(self, req: EffectiveRequirement) -> RequirementResearch:
        out = RequirementResearch(requirement_id=req.requirement_id)
        report = None
        until = self._until(MATERIAL_SECONDS)
        searches: list[dict] = []  # what the search worker's site_tools.search calls showed, over both attempts
        for attempt in range(2):  # retry once: the ERP sometimes drops the session mid-search
            if self.left() < MATERIAL_SECONDS + 20:
                break
            async with self._slot():
                session = await self._worker_tab(req.requirement_id if not attempt else f"{req.requirement_id}+")
                if session is None:
                    continue
                try:
                    report = await self._search(session, req, until, searches)
                finally:
                    await self._close(session)
            if report is not None or group_without_hits(searches, req.catalog_group):
                break  # a result, or the site said the group has no hits (another attempt would see the same)
        if (report is None or not report.candidates) and group_without_hits(searches, req.catalog_group):
            out.search_term = report.search_term if report else req.catalog_group
            out.no_hits = True  # searched, no match (rule 3), not a gap
            self.trace.event("erp", "group_without_hits", requirement=req.requirement_id,
                             searches=[{k: v for k, v in x.items() if k != "text"} for x in searches])

                                    mounting=c.mounting, certification=c.certification)
                          for c in report.candidates]
        # every hit of the model's search is inspected (the rules cap a usable search at 20 hits), those whose rows
        # fit the requirement as known now first; which one fits is the model's choice below, once details are known
        first, rest = inspection_order(req, out.candidates)
        out.inspected = first + rest
        hits = len(dict.fromkeys(c.material_number for c in out.candidates))
        if hits > len(out.inspected):

        out.problems.append(UNFINISHED)

class Trace:
    def __init__(self, directory: str | None = None):
        global CURRENT
        CURRENT = self
        self.key: list[str] = []
        self.reader_metrics = dict(completed=0, fallbacks=0, cells=0,
                                   calls=0, input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0)
        self.started = self.last = time.monotonic()
        directory = directory or os.environ.get("TRACE_DIR", "traces")
        Path(directory).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # events that mark a phase or a failure; repeated in one block at the end of the run (summary())
    KEY_KINDS = {"start", "done", "stopped", "problem", "start_failed", "spec_done", "tender_facts", "mail_kind",
                 "answer", "summary_check", "last_chance", "crashed", "decision_disputed", "helper_error",

                 "qa_incomplete", "tender_qa", "no_bid_recheck_done", "no_bid_overturned"}

    def event(self, worker: str, kind: str, quiet: bool = False, **data) -> None:
        if kind == 'reader_code_fallback':
            self.reader_metrics['fallbacks'] += 1
        elif kind == 'reader_code_cell' or kind == 'reader_code_finish':
            self.reader_metrics['cells'] += 1
        elif kind == 'reader_code_done':
            self.reader_metrics['completed'] += 1
            for field in ('calls', 'input_tokens', 'output_tokens'):
                self.reader_metrics[field] += data.get(field, 0)

        seconds = round(self.last - self.started, 2)
        self.file.write(json.dumps({"t": seconds, "worker": worker, "kind": kind, **data}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        self.file.flush()
        if quiet:  # file only, e.g. the full page views
            return
        brief = " ".join(f"{k}={str(v)[:120]!r}" if isinstance(v, str) else f"{k}={v}" for k, v in data.items())
        print(f"[{seconds:7.1f}s] {worker:<15} {kind:<12} {brief}", flush=True)
        if kind in self.KEY_KINDS:
            self.key.append(f"[{seconds:7.1f}s] {worker:<15} {kind:<12} {brief[:150]}")

def to_position_input(position: str, quantity: int, unit: str | calc.Unit, requirement: Requirement,
                      material: MaterialRecord | None, pieces_per_set: int | None = None,
                      **extra) -> calc.PositionInput:
    """One position for calc: quantity in its stated unit (from the tender worker), pieces per set (an amended value
    from `effective_requirement` when given, else the spec's), the ERP material and its price conditions. `extra`
    passes the Q&A/mail facts (discount_scope, setup_fee, packaging, commitment) through."""
    return calc.PositionInput(
        position=position, quantity=quantity, unit=unit if isinstance(unit, calc.Unit) else calc.parse_unit(unit),
        pieces_per_set=pieces_per_set or requirement.pieces_per_set,
        material=material.to_material() if material else None,
        conditions=material.conditions if material else [], **extra)
            self.started_at = time.monotonic()
        if req.requirement_id not in self.tasks:
            self.tasks[req.requirement_id] = asyncio.create_task(self.requirement(req))
        return self.tasks[req.requirement_id]

    async def collect(self) -> ErpResearch:
        """Wait for every started requirement and the materials they inspect (each ends by the deadline)."""
        results = []
        for k in sorted(self.tasks, key=calc.position_key):
            try:
                results.append(await self.tasks[k])
            except Exception as error:  # one failed requirement must not cost the others
                results.append(RequirementResearch(requirement_id=k, problems=[
                    f"research failed: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}"]))
        return ErpResearch(requirements=results, materials=self.records(),
                           seconds=round(time.monotonic() - (self.started_at or time.monotonic()), 1))

    def records(self) -> dict[str, MaterialRecord]:
        """Every material record finished so far."""
        out = {}
        for number, task in self.materials.items():
            if not task.done() or task.cancelled():
                continue
            if task.exception() is not None:
                self.trace.event("erp", "material_failed", material=number, error=type(task.exception()).__name__)
            elif task.result() is not None:
                out[number] = task.result()
        return out

    async def research(self, requirements: list[EffectiveRequirement]) -> ErpResearch:
        for req in requirements:
            self.start(req)
        return await self.collect()

Current optimizations do **not** provide a credible route to 4.7× lower cost and 9.2× lower time. That requires removing entire classes of model turns.

Measured evidence:

- Broad Python readers consumed only 6.7% of full-run input in their latest trial; all seven fell back. Perfect elimination of that work would still leave most of the gap.
- Shared discovery selected zero URLs. Its lower whole-run input does not demonstrate successful discovery savings.
- The supplied private batch trial emitted no batch events. It therefore did not measure the intended mechanism.
- The bounded run’s output alone cost $0.02473, exceeding the leader’s $0.0233 total. Reducing source input without drastically reducing turns and output cannot reach that budget. [Evidence and cost breakdown](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/docs/radical-efficiency-plan.md:11)

The largest concrete restructuring candidate is **repeated navigation over similar ERP material records**. [Erp._material](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/research.py:1265) starts a browser worker for each material, permits 6–18 model requests, then separately invokes a material reader; incomplete records can repeat the process. Material tasks already share a cache by number, so adding a simple material cache would duplicate existing functionality.

My architectural hypothesis: let the model establish a reusable layout mapping and choose the material links and relevant views, then execute that bounded selection through code. Reuse the mapping across selected records; return compact typed facts with source references; ask the model again when controls, structure or evidence differ. This moves repeated mechanical navigation and copying out of the model. It must remain model-directed and satisfy the repository’s fair-play contract. Its savings are presently unmeasured.

Mail has the same structural problem: [research_kind](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/research_mail.py:578) launches a fresh [thinking search worker](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/research_mail.py:519) for each kind, repeating folder/search operations. The known retained 80 calls make this another substantial candidate. A runtime search-control mapping with model-selected queries is more testable than asking one enlarged worker to discover every commercial kind. The failed shared sweep does not establish that repeated search execution is unavoidable.

There is also genuinely removable decision work: [check_choice](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/evidence.py:467) already computes exact eligibility. For a complete requirement with exactly one inspected active match, code can select that match directly instead of calling [choose_material](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/research.py:1373). Preserve semantic wording checks, multiple-match handling and incomplete-evidence handling. This is a smaller, defensible improvement; its whole-run share is unknown.

The minimum useful experiment is one ERP layout mapping reused across several model-selected materials. Compare it against the existing material workers on the same private layout after the scope fix. Require equivalent complete records, submitted quality, and fewer navigation calls **including mapping and fallback**. First retain complete per-phase calls, uncached/cached input, output and durations: the current [trace summary](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/tracing.py:57) can omit intermediate workers, so retained tail counts cannot identify the largest billed phase reliably.

At the documented rates, an illustrative target of **90,000 uncached input + 350,000 cached input + 7,000 output** costs **$0.02239**. That is a design constraint, not a forecast. The 49-second goal additionally requires measuring and shrinking the actual serial path through research, form completion and TAN signing. Four browsers and lower token counts alone do not establish that timing.

I inspected source and experiment documentation only; no modifications or tests were run.

This moves repeated mechanical navigation and copying out of the model. It must remain model-directed and satisfy the repository’s fair-play contract. Its savings are presently unmeasured.

Mail has the same structural problem: [research_kind](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/research_mail.py:578) launches a fresh [thinking search worker](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/research_mail.py:519) for each kind, repeating folder/search operations. The known retained 80 calls make this another substantial candidate. A runtime search-control mapping with model-selected queries is more testable than asking one enlarged worker to discover every commercial kind. The failed shared sweep does not establish that repeated search execution is unavoidable.

There is also genuinely removable decision work: [check_choice](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/evidence.py:467) already computes exact eligibility. For a complete requirement with exactly one inspected active match, code can select that match directly instead of calling [choose_material](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/research.py:1373). Preserve semantic wording checks, multiple-match handling and incomplete-evidence handling. This is a smaller, defensible improvement; its whole-run share is unknown.

The minimum useful experiment is one ERP layout mapping reused across several model-selected materials. Compare it against the existing material workers on the same private layout after the scope fix. Require equivalent complete records, submitted quality, and fewer navigation calls **including mapping and fallback**. First retain complete per-phase calls, uncached/cached input, output and durations: the current [trace summary](/private/tmp/ehl-reader-kernel/agent/tracing.py:57) can omit intermediate workers, so retained tail counts cannot identify the largest billed phase reliably.

At the documented rates, an illustrative target of **90,000 uncached input + 350,000 cached input + 7,000 output** costs **$0.02239**. That is a design constraint, not a forecast. The 49-second goal additionally requires measuring and shrinking the actual serial path through research, form completion and TAN signing. Four browsers and lower token counts alone do not establish that timing.

I inspected source and experiment documentation only; no modifications or tests were run.
